alternatives_rejected.why: The CPU spike is real, but a CPU-only fault would not make diskio jump from a near-zero baseline (z~9.6e18, E1/E3). Disk stress accounts for both the disk and the CPU signal. One caveat: a z-score that large partly reflects a near-zero baseline variance, so it shows disk I/O appeared but overstates how big the change is.

alternatives_rejected.candidate: checkoutservice: upstream caller inflating email latency
alternatives_rejected.why: The all-services ranking in E1 shows significant deviations only on emailservice metrics. E2 shows callers seeing emailservice slow down 2.75x (3.49->9.61ms) at emailservice itself, not at checkout.

proposed_fix.description: Find and stop the process or workload generating excessive disk I/O in the emailservice pod. If that is not possible, restart or reschedule the emailservice pod onto a healthy node. Then confirm diskio, cpu and caller-observed latency return to baseline.
